title: 01. RAG Foundations: Naive RAG vs Advanced RAG vs Modular RAG
summary: RAG has evolved through three generations. Naive RAG (2020-2022) is the basic retrieve-then-read pipeline: embed query → ANN search → stuff top-K chunks into prompt → generate.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: RAG has evolved through three generations. **Naive RAG** (2020-2022) is the basic retrieve-then-read pipeline: embed query → ANN search → stuff top-K chunks into prompt → generate. It works but suffers from retrieval quality issues, chunk boundary problems, and no feedback loops. **Advanced RAG** (2023-2024) introduces pre-retrieval improvements (query rewriting, HyDE), post-retrieval improvements (reranking, contextual compression), and iterative retrieval (Self-RAG, CRAG). **Modular RAG** (2024-2026) treats each component — retriever, ranker, reader, memory, router — as an independent, swappable module in a pipeline. This enables hybrid strategies: route factual queries to dense retrieval, aggregate queries to SQL, comparison queries to multi-hop chains. In 2026, production systems are universally Modular RAG architectures orchestrated via LangGraph or LlamaIndex Workflows.

diagrams.title: Naive → Advanced → Modular RAG
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TB
  subgraph N["Naive RAG"]
    n1["retrieve top-k"] --> n2["generate"]
  end
  subgraph A["Advanced RAG"]
    a0["query rewrite"] --> a1["hybrid retrieve"] --> a2["rerank"] --> a3["compress"] --> a4["generate + cite"]
  end
  subgraph M["Modular RAG"]
    m0{"router"} --> m1["vector search"]
    m0 --> m2["SQL / API"]
    m0 --> m3["graph search"]
    m1 --> m4["grade + retry loop"]
    m2 --> m4
    m3 --> m4
    m4 --> m5["generate"]
  end
diagrams.explain: **Naive RAG** is retrieve-then-generate. **Advanced RAG** adds steps around retrieval: rewrite the query before, rerank and compress after. **Modular RAG** treats each step as a swappable module and adds routing and feedback loops (grade, retry), which is the bridge to agentic RAG.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
EVOLUTION: Naive → Advanced → Modular RAG
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

NAIVE RAG (2020-2022)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query ──▶ Embed ──▶ ANN Search ──▶ Top-5 Chunks ──▶ LLM ──▶ Answer
          (raw)    (one shot)    (no filtering)   (basic)

Problems: Poor queries, redundant chunks, no quality check

ADVANCED RAG (2023-2024)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
         ┌─ Query Rewriting ─┐
Query ───┤  HyDE             ├──▶ ANN Search ──▶ Retrieve 20
         └─ Multi-query     ─┘                        │
                                                       ▼
                                                  Reranker
                                                       │
                                                       ▼
                                              Contextual Compress
                                                       │
                                              ┌────────▼────────┐
                                              │   LLM + Top-5   │──▶ Answer
                                              └─────────────────┘
                                              (with CRAG re-retrieval
                                               if confidence < threshold)

MODULAR RAG (2024-2026)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

                          ┌─────────────┐
                          │   Router    │
              ┌──────────▶│  (LangGraph │
              │           │   node)     │
Query ──▶ Classifier      └──────┬──────┘
                                 │
              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
              ▼                  ▼                  ▼
         Dense Vector        SQL Engine         Graph RAG
         Retrieval           (for counts)       (for relations)
              │                  │                  │
              └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                                 ▼
                            Fusion / Merge
                                 │
                            ┌────▼────┐
                            │  LLM    │──▶ Answer + Citations
                            └─────────┘
```

quiz.question: What is Modular RAG and how does it differ from Advanced RAG?
options: Prompt stuffing: $500-5,000/month (token costs). Fine-tuning: $10,000-50,000 training cost amortized + inference.
Document ingestion pipeline** with chunking and embedding, (2) Vector store for semantic retrieval, (3) Embedding model (consistent between index and query), (4)…
Users phrase queries colloquially ("what's the return window?") while documents use formal language ("merchandise returns are accepted within 30 calendar days").
Advanced RAG improves a fixed pipeline; Modular RAG decouples the pipeline into composable modules with defined interfaces.
quiz.explanation: Advanced RAG improves a fixed pipeline; Modular RAG decouples the pipeline into composable modules with defined interfaces. Each module can be independently replaced, scaled, or A/B tested. A Modular RAG system might: route factual queries to dense retrieval, structured queries to SQL, knowledge graph queries to a graph engine — all within the same system.
